_about: Open plots, plants and payoffs, as data (GM only). A thread: id, title, truth (T#), feeds, status open|paid, who_knows (the knowledge state the page has established), note (the GM's running note), on_page (the block keys where it was planted or touched: rebuilt by the engine from the events' thread touches; a truth needs two before any scene reveals it). Written through `saga.py record` (a block's note names the threads it touched or changed) and `saga.py threads`; read through `saga.py threads` and `saga.py brief`, never whole.

threads.title: Aldric said *"Ride wide today"* and almost said more; his horse was turned and climbing the west bank one heartbeat before the Grace failed
threads.who_knows: Darrow; the reader. Maelis knows only that he believes the Grace was taken, no name. Marrant has read, and Aldric will read, Darrow's order of the ford in his own hand. 04:s2: Darrow, Wren, Hollis, Anselm and Rae saw that the clerk's hand on Mirren's letter is the hand that addressed Aldric's letters; Rae has seen the hand elsewhere and will not say where
threads.note: touched 03:s3 (the letter to Aldric). 04:s2 (T3 plant): the direction on Aldric's three letters and Mirren's letter are in one clerk's hand, the clerk at the winch-house who never kneels: Vane's household and the Confessors write with one hand. Darrow has joined the two letters; he has not said Vane's name over it

threads.title: The writ to charge: Hollis broke the seal with his thumb without looking at it. Where is that paper now?
threads.who_knows: Hollis knows where his own is and has never looked at its seal; the page has shown him look at a blue seal on Marrant's writ at the bars and watch the blue wax of Darrow's letters (02:s5, 03:s2), saying nothing; Darrow knows (03:between-3) Hollis kept the writ and has never looked at its seal, not where it is; the reader (the leg's cup, 01:interlude)
threads.note: active: paper in the cup of Hollis's wooden leg, seal unexamined; the writ at the bars wore blue wax the size of a child's palm (the first of the two wax plants q1.letters needs; his own still unlooked-at until b2.4)

threads.title: The clan line was drawn up wrong: carts, old people, children; warriors looking behind them into the trees
threads.who_knows: Darrow suspects they were fleeing; Hollis heard it and dismissed it; the reader
threads.note: Darrow suspects they were fleeing. **Revised 10/11 (editorial pass):** after Hollis said mount up, Darrow chose the line over the carts himself ("a question for whoever had put the wax on Hollis's paper"); he carries that, not the heralds' sin. Never a confession to anyone yet; T5 stays Book III

threads.title: Grey armored figures standing motionless among the Thornwild trees, unmoved by the slaughter
threads.who_knows: Darrow saw them; the red-handed woman made him look; the reader
threads.note: unexplained

threads.title: The red-handed woman pulled Darrow out and said *"Look. Remember it."*
threads.who_knows: Darrow; the reader. He does not know her name
threads.note: he doesn't know her name

threads.title: Maelis: the knee "had help for twelve" years (the Grace carried it)
threads.who_knows: Maelis knows what she means; Darrow has the words and not the why; the reader likewise
threads.note: touched Ch 1 Sc 2: "It has none now. What holds it is you." Still unexplained

threads.title: Maelis on how many Bindings she's done: *"Enough to know what the soft season looks like."*
threads.who_knows: Maelis; Darrow suspects a past and saw the Confessor look; Marrant suspects (GM: he is fishing for her); the reader. 03:s4: Darrow saw her walk the undercroft dark without a lamp and put the lintel into plain speech, counted the unmarked flour, the unturned key and the unwalked stair, and concluded there is another way down that she knows
threads.note: 03:climax (T8 plant): she did not say up until the wrist ('I wanted to see if you'd go'); 'the second time I've seen a hand go into one of those. The first man kept his.' She has a past with these stones, said aloud for the first time; what she was is still unsaid

threads.title: The List. Confessors on the Holloway: six men, a cart, a censer. Darrow first, Hollis second
threads.who_knows: The whole House, kitchen included; the valley got the lie (c01.1) and Marrant climbed anyway (c01.1b fired); the reader. Nobody in grey knows Darrow's face: Marrant called for the Captain of the Ninth to the whole court
threads.note: **b1.1 done at the Ch 1 climax (10/11, Costly):** Marrant named at the bars; the far cots not read ("The Crown has no quarrel with men who can't answer"); Marrant plus four at the bars, the sixth below with Rae's cart; the Prior stalled at the wicket for the bell until Marrant made refusing a courier a breach of the law of guests; two grey cloaks through and a third holding it, a lay brother bloodied, Darrow's shoulder could not shut it (Might fail), the lay brothers', the gate-ward's and Rae's did; the two inside walked the wounded looking at faces and passed Darrow close enough to touch without knowing him; Old Mercy late (Pell's hands: b1.5's hinge planted a second time, and Marrant noticed: "A fine bell. A little slow on the rope."); the Prior spoke the law of names (lore house.law_of_bells fully spoken); Marrant's eyes on Maelis (T8); camp on the lower terrace; the call to come down and kneel. Darrow's Insight succeeded (the timing was his: "Wren. Now."), his Resolve failed (the flinch: Wren's hand on his sleeve, Hollis's sound in his beard, nobody else). **Choice answered 10/11: option 1, step forward** (c01.5, `named_himself`; candor +2 → Candor/Guile −1, even; Maelis +8, Wren −7, Hollis +3, Rae +2 banked; confessors −5): he crossed the court, called Marrant back from the head of the Steps by both names, gave his own and his rank, and killed the valley's story himself ('You've read to a full bed'); Marrant looked at his face (he has it now), called him Captain, and thanked the *Prior* for her candour (the arc's barb, aimed where the Downstream puts it); the Prior did not reproach Darrow and asked whether the shoulder was hurt (the Downstream's 'which is worse', shown); Wren: hidden for as long as it takes to count to eleven; Hollis: he saw the flinch at the name and nobody else did, then 'Captain', meant; Maelis approved in her coin, with her reason on the page (revised 10/11): 'Hidden, you were a lie they'd have found by the thaw. Named, you're a law they'll have to break where the valley can watch.' then 'That knee lies to me every morning. You didn't. Keep it that way.' (she knows naming points them at the knee, and judges the law safer than the lie); Darrow's own reasons are on the page too: every face in the House read for his, the lie already dead, the bell already rung and will read the knee tonight (ch02:s1: the Knots held; the real knee was clean the next morning). Due: c01.5c at ch02:s1 (the writ's demand personal, by rank), c01.5a at b1.5 (the Prior refuses for a named man), c01.5b in Book II (the Lowmarch heard; faithless +5). Earlier: the council (Sc 3), the lie to the valley (c01.1, guile +1; c01.1a fired Sc 4), Sc 4 (the bell held; the timing handed to Darrow; the grey cloaks in at the winch-house three bells early)

threads.title: The far cots: the Hollowed breathing in the dark; one was Wren's mother (not yet said on the page)
threads.who_knows: The page has only 'the far cots'; Wren, Maelis and the Prior know whose (GM); Darrow and the reader do not. 03:s4: Darrow and Maelis saw Wren read the old hand over the undercroft's inner door straight off and stop halfway; nobody has asked her how; Hollis and the Prior did not see it
threads.note: background. 03:s4 (T6 plant): Wren read 'What is given can be taken' over the inner door and stopped; Maelis finished it and told her not in the hall; Wren read none of the murals for him and shut her ledger on the line for the door

threads.title: Tobin Marsh, 19, sang badly and constantly; went under at the ford while Darrow turned toward him (revised 10/11: his hand came up beyond Thistle's neck; when Darrow surfaced there was only water where it had been)
threads.who_knows: Darrow; the reader; Marrant (read it) and Aldric (when it reaches him), from Darrow's letter, that he turned toward Tobin. Rae carted his bundle (GM; not on the page).
threads.note: Darrow hasn't said his name aloud; he wrote it in his answer to Aldric (03:s3), with Thistle's.

threads.title: Benedek Orrin introduced. Hollis's Sixth, not yet thirty, spear through the shoulder, fever, says his oath at every bell and claims he still feels the warmth; offered Hollis the heralds' mercy
threads.who_knows: The reader has his oath and his claim of warmth; Hollis's kind lie is known to Hollis and the reader, not to Benedek; that he knelt anew is on no page yet (GM). The House knows (02:climax) he said his oath at the first three bells of the night he was taken and not at the fourth
threads.note: on the page; Hollis lied to him kindly; Between 4: the Captain said the oath's words with him, lips only, no sound (c01.3: he expects it at the bells now; Hollis saw; c01.3a fired Sc 4). **Not named at the gate**: the page has not yet said so in his hearing; his relief is Ch 2 Sc 1 (the night of the gate), and the Grey Cot is Ch 2 Sc 2, the feast morning (b1.2) 03:s7: at the noon oath the lad's frost neither grew nor melted; Hollis carried his blanket to the stair head.

threads.title: Hollis has thought for a fortnight of teaching the Captain to fight from a chair; and he is two days without a drink with nobody to tell
threads.feeds: Seated Blade, Hollis's arc; q1.wager's bottle still unspoken
threads.who_knows: The chair: Hollis only; the reader. The drink: Hollis, Darrow (Between 3), the reader; not Benedek, not Maelis
threads.note: the drink told (c01.2, approval +2; c01.2a fired at the climax: his hands steady on the gatehouse sill because he held them so, and after the Choice Darrow looked at them and did not ask how he was); the chair still planted; the bottle he hasn't opened belongs to q1.wager and has not been mentioned. Choice: he saw the Captain flinch at his name, told him nobody else had, and called him Captain, meant

threads.title: Rae Thorne on the page. The carter of the last cart (talked to her oxen, said "Aye" to Hollis, looked at his leg like a cracked wheel, rang her bell and a bell answered; "They'll count you up. Don't help."); heard the list read at Coldmere, climbed through the night to bring it up; her cart and two oxen stand at the winch-house, which Darrow knew from the window
threads.who_knows: The House knows she brought the list; Darrow has her one line and her question; the reader
threads.note: 04:between-1: her wants in her own words (the debt on the cart and oxen to her uncle at the inn, paid by the load; to carry a thing up and see it come down whole); 'I keep the faces'; one question a night, the dawn a new one; 'Road's the road' spoken; she took the mare's name down

threads.title: Thistle. The grey mare went down in the Wend; the codex says fate unknown. (GM: alive, lame, a Holloway dealer's at Coldmere; Rae has fed her and asks whether the captain rode a grey)
threads.who_knows: Rae knows the mare lives and where; Darrow knows it from her and that the dealer holds her on his name till the thaw (04:s2); he said her name, Thistle, to Rae at the wicket (04:between-1); Wren and Hollis heard of the mare; the reader
threads.note: Tale 1 p1: the long grey mare in the far field, unnamed; piece 2 names the filly out of her for the thistles. 03:s5 (q1.cart stage 2): Rae on the cage head: a grey mare at a dealer's on the Holloway, out of the Wend below the ford, short behind, won't take a bridge forwards (the Calden bridge, codex); the price is the dealer's debt at Coldmere, 'more than a shirt and a stick'. 04:s2 (c03.6a paid): the dealer took his name: the mare's keep till the thaw, then coin or sold on. 04:between-1: he said her name to Rae ('Her name's Thistle'), the first time since the water; Rae: 'I'll tell her.' The finding is Tether III; the thaw is its clock

threads.title: Marrant at the gate. Confessor Ivo Marrant named at the bars; Marrant and four grey cloaks camped on the lower terrace, the sixth at the winch-house; he has noticed the bell is slow on the rope; his demand to the court: the Captain of the Ninth comes down and kneels and the rest of the paper goes back in his cloak; "Bells grow tired"; "I'll wait. It's the thing I'm best at."
threads.feeds: b1.2 (he names the Hollowing witchcraft and asks for the Mender by title), q1.letters stage 2 (he carries the second letter up), b1.5
threads.who_knows: The whole House heard it; the reader. Marrant has the Captain's voice and his face at the bars now (c01.5): the demand is personal. What he wants (Maelis) and his plan (b1.2 Benedek, b1.4 Anselm, b1.5 Old Mercy) are GM only; his look at Maelis is thread 7. The camp's measure (flour for six to the thaw and past it, out of Coldmere; the House's wood) is Rae's count, said to Darrow on the page (02:s4); a grey cloak keeps the winch-house byre door.
threads.note: the siege's first night; the kitchen's loaves and the feast's bread under his eyes are Ch 2's first world moves. 02:s4: the grey cloak on Rae's box got down for her without a word; the camp has flour to the thaw and past it; the first letter came up with Rae.

threads.title: The black glass under Benedek's tongue: still cold after three days in Maelis's coat; Darrow says it looks like a chip off a field-stone, and she did not say no; she keeps it, and asked him to keep it out of the hall
threads.truth: Oathstone: frost drawn out of a man too fast leaves a sliver of the stone it went to (arc b1.2, T1); the far cots, drained slowly over years, never had one
threads.feeds: T1, b1.3 (the shard drawing on the wounded above)
threads.who_knows: Maelis keeps the chip and suspects (T1); Darrow has now seen the rest of the stone in the wall under the row, knows it came up in the satchel and that a hand set it (03:climax), and says it is the same glass as the chip; Wren saw it and was stopped before naming the almoner; Hollis saw the hand and the slab, and has asked; the Prior saw the slab and the hand and asked nothing; the whole lit row saw them come up; the reader
threads.note: 03:climax (Hard-won): the lid of mortar off in one piece; the sliver seen on end with frost in straight lines from its foot; 'It came up in the satchel'; the frost to his knuckles, then held; the shard is one with the rock: it stays. The chip and the sliver joined aloud by Darrow ('here was the rest of the stone'). The lid with the thumbprint is on the linen press: evidence that can be shown or hidden

threads.title: Rae's calling: a wick of the Lantern Market (six years on the north road), posted to the House's carting; sent since midsummer for what the Order carries up the mountain
threads.truth: A wick carries, never keeps; she keeps the mare, the aye, the letter and him. The corner shows at q2.lantern, the calling at b3.4, the recall in Book IV, the price in Book VI (rae.road, _gm/characters.md, _gm/world.md 5a).
threads.feeds: q1.cart, q2.lantern, b3.4, q4.censer, q5.second, q6.market, r.b6.rae_door
threads.who_knows: Rae; her uncle Hale, the lamp at Coldmere; nobody at the House; the reader has her tells only (the bow off her box, the camp read by flour, the letter inside her shirt, name-the-load, the cold in her cart, one question a night)
threads.note: Plants already on the page before this thread was opened, counted by eye (the engine counts from here): 02:s4, 02:interlude, 02:between-10, 02:between-11, 02:climax. Next plants: q1.cart stage 2 (the satchel's weights), b1.4 (the clerk's first climb), b1.5 (the second line). No reveal before Book III.

threads.title: The mural under the House: a knight kneeling at a black stone, the light running up out of him along a thread into the vault, where the standing figures hold theirs over their open hands
threads.feeds: T7, b1.3 climax (the murals by tier)
threads.who_knows: Darrow, Wren and Maelis saw it; the reader. Nobody has said what it means; Maelis knows (T7)
threads.note: 03:s4 planted: 'The others held theirs. His went up.' Darrow tried the strokes beside the knight's head and got nothing; Wren did not read them.

threads.title: The clerk in grey at the winch-house: an older man with a desk on two kegs who writes the Confessors' letters and never kneels at the dawn bell; he gave the almoner two slivers before the snow and called them the Spire's mercy for the wounded
threads.who_knows: Anselm (he saw him); Darrow, Hollis, Maelis, Wren and the Prior have it from Anselm's confession (04:s1); the reader. Marrant knows his own clerk. The clerk's name is not on the page
threads.note: 04:s1 planted: 'I never saw him kneel.' The lie he told Anselm (a stone takes the fever through the floor, as at the Spire) is the truth turned inside out. 04:s2: his hand on Mirren's letter is the hand that addressed Aldric's three letters (T3: Vane's secretary); 'He writes all of them'
